speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, please take a seat. I see you have a concerning rash and recent health changes; to help me understand your condition, could you describe exactly where the rash is located and when it first appeared? Additionally, have you experienced any fever, fatigue, or changes in your weight lately?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with a rash that started last night, finding it very concerning. He does not recall being exposed to any new environmental stimuli such as detergents or plants like poison ivy. He mentions he recently started seeing a primary care provider for arthritis management and a new onset cough.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. The rash appearing suddenly alongside a new cough and a visit for arthritis management is a significant cluster of symptoms. Could you describe the specific appearance of the rash (e.g., redness, bumps, blisters) and whether it is itchy or painful? Also, when did the cough begin and is it productive?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on the upper half of the back. I also have Concern over sudden onset, Recent cough, Unaware of exposure to new environmental stimuli, Mucositis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Sulfonamide Drug Eruption (Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis) likely precipitated by a new medication for arthritis and/or an infection.

REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology full body scan.
